riley (devex): FYI found a flaky duplicate during mobile onboarding when retries, 429 handling, and auth refresh all mixed. Posting the minimal repro + asking for mobile-SDK guidance on safe resume/backoff.

samir (mobile-sdk): can you share where you persist the pending work on mobile? Async storage / sqlite?

riley (devex): We persist a JSON blob in AsyncStorage including full payload + idempotencyKey so the UI can retry after crash. On app resume we immediately POST the saved body.

ada (platform): storing full body is risky for both privacy and duplicates. If a token rotate/refresh happens while the original request is still being processed, a replay can create a duplicate resource.

riley (devex): Timeline: t0 POST /purchase -> t1 network hiccup -> t2 app triggers token refresh -> t3 resume logic re-POSTs stored payload -> t4 original completes with 201 -> t5 replay returns 201 -> duplicate charge.

samir (mobile-sdk): For mobile UX: persist only minimal pending metadata (idempKey, endpoint, timestamp, optional resourceIdHint). On resume do NOT immediately re-POST. Instead: 1) if you have a resourceIdHint, check its status; 2) otherwise call a HEAD /idemp/:key endpoint to detect completion; 3) treat 202 as in-flight and poll; 4) only POST if check says missing.

riley (devex): Is it safe to treat 202 as in-progress always? Some backends return 202 for queued but may never materialize if the job errors later.

ada (platform): 202 means "accepted" not "completed"; you must poll status or subscribe to a webhook. SDK guidance should differentiate accepted vs final states and encourage polling frequency limits.

samir (mobile-sdk): We'll add helpers: `mobileSdk.idempotency.check(key)` and `mobileSdk.resumePending(pending, {graceMs, maxPolls})`. resumePending will: subscribe to auth events, on resume if refresh is in-flight wait up to graceMs then call check; if in_progress poll with exponential backoff; if missing create new attempt with new idempotency key.

riley (devex): What about 429s? Our mobile client aggressively retries on 429 with a small decorrelated jitter which might exacerbate duplication during auth storms.

samir (mobile-sdk): Recommend full jitter for 429s: sleep = rand(0, base * 2^attempt). Also, when an auth refresh is observed, temporarily increase base multiplier to spread retries. Example: base=300ms, auth-refresh-multiplier=3 -> gives breathing room.

ada (platform): Also suggest adding a client-namespace prefix to keys, e.g., `deviceId:key`, so server dedupe windows can be scoped. And servers should expose an optional `X-Original-Idempotency` header support to reconcile recreate attempts.

riley (devex): For mobile storage, any guidance on persisting bodies encrypted? We can't leak PII.

samir (mobile-sdk): Strongly recommend never persisting raw bodies with PII. If unavoidable, encrypt with platform keystore and keep TTL small. Prefer storing only the idempotency marker and resource hint instead. We'll add a warning in the quickstart.

ada (platform): Small server-side note: document dedupe retention window (e.g., 5 minutes) and whether 202 transitions to final state asynchronously. That helps clients choose poll timeouts and grace windows.

riley (devex): OK I'll change the mobile sampleapp: persist only {idempotencyKey, endpoint, resourceHint, createdAt}, on resume call `mobileSdk.resumePending(pending, {graceMs:1500, maxPolls:5})`. If check returns missing then create new attempt with new key and set header `X-Original-Idempotency:oldKey`.

samir (mobile-sdk): Perfect. I'll open a small PR adding resumePending + check helper, include a short snippet for full jitter 429 strategy, and add auth event hooks. Also will add a short e2e test simulating token rotation + 429.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapps/mobile-onboarding #221 started tests :runner:

riley (devex): Thanks — tagging the PR with "mobile-idempotency". One last UX note: keep the UI in "Submitting..." state until final confirmation or show a clear "Submission pending" screen so users don't tap Submit twice.

ada (platform): Good call. And add a small server fallback note: if backend lacks idempotency-check, clients should pause for grace window then re-POST with new key but accept some risk; document this limitation.

samir (mobile-sdk): We'll include that fallback in the helper docs. OK I'll write the RFC and PR today.

riley (devex): Awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
